findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizer bucket (quaternary ammonia) for food contact surfaces to be at a low concentration. CORRECTED- sanitizer bucket was remade to 400 ppm. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made and tested at a frequency to reach the sanitizing concentration for food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacturer’s label (200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the ambient thermometer in the under counter cooler to be broken. Ensure all cooling units holding temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods contain a working ambient thermometer to monitor cold holding temperatures. Obtain an ambient thermometer for this unit by 4/6/26.
findings.citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: A bin of water was observed in the walk-in cooler on the top shelf directly across from the door. There is a small drip from the vent in the ceiling. Repair the cooler to eliminate the leak. See that condensation drainage is discharged and is not dripping back into the walk-in cooler.
findings.citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the self closer to the men’s restroom to be nonfunctioning. Ensure the self closer is repaired by the next routine inspection. Restrooms should have functioning self closing doors to protect against food contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Several physical facilities violations have remained from the pre-opening:
1) 2ND REPEAT: Acoustic tiles were observed above the passageway between the cold line and the kitchen. Eliminate use of acoustic tiles. Replace them with vinyl coated or wipeable tiles.
2) 2ND REPEAT: Replace broken floor tiles by mop sink & grease trap. Broken tiles allow buildup of general debris and water.
3) FIRST REPEAT: Several holes were observed in the wall behind the 3 compartment sink. Fill or patch any holes.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Multiple areas within the physical facilities were observed to have coving separating from the wall:
1) 2ND REPEAT:the wall near the entrance to the kitchen.
2) To the left of the hand washing sink (nearest the register). 
3) To the left of the mop sink
4) On the side counter between the soda machine and self service drink cooler.
Ensure coving is sealed to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a significant accumulation of food and other soil debris on the floor drain beneath the 3 compartment sink. Physical facilities should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris. Discussed doing an initial deep clean, then maintaining cleanliness every 2 weeks. Floor drains are a significant source of harborage for pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed one dim light present in the facility’s walk in cooler. Replace this lightbulb to display an intensity of at least 108 lux by the next routine inspection. Food areas must be adequately lit.
findings.citation_text: 6-303.11(A) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning; [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: It was observed that no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM/CFM) was on site during today’s inspection. The only employee present had a Food Handler’s card. All Class II facilities must have a CFM present during all times at which food is handled or prepared. The presence of a CFM helps to decrease the risk of food-borne illness by overseeing safe food handling practices, and ensuring temperatures of all Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) items are within their required range (below 41F or above 135F) to prevent the growth of harmful pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The inspector observed a gap between the floor and wall between the soda machine and standing drink cooler. This gap may allow for the collection of food and other debris. Debris may attract pests. Reseal coving by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Sliced tomatoes in the front line veggie cooler were observed at 49F (probed). Other TCS foods in the cooler were observed in temperature (see Temperature Observations). CORRECTED- Sliced tomatoes were voluntarily discarded. Continue to monitor foods in the veggie prep cooler to ensure they are held at 41F or below. Ice accumulation was observed around some pans in this cooler, which may contribute to uneven cooling.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]
